messages:
anna (support): customer reports 502s from hosted inference API since ~09:12 UTC, high error rate, escalation requested

james (platform): thanks — which tenant / request-id examples? any recent deploys?

anna (support): tenant: tenant-acme, sample request ids: req_01G9X2J0, req_01G9X2K7, one shows upstream 502 via gateway. No deploys on their side. Billing spike noted around same time.

samir (runtime): looking at control-plane traces — routing-policy svc started returning 504s at 09:11; configdb started throwing connection timeouts shortly after. Could be connection pool exhaustion.

maya (oncall): I'm oncall - i pulled recent control-plane logs. snippet: ```
2026-03-17T09:10:58Z routing-policy[pid=72] ERROR fetchRoutes timeout=3000ms tenant=tenant-acme
2026-03-17T09:11:02Z configdb[pool-3] WARN conn_acquire_timeout tenant=tenant-acme waiting=2500ms
2026-03-17T09:11:05Z auth-session[pid=11] ERROR session-validate 5xx upstream=502 upstream_req=req_01G9X2J0
```

anna (support): customer mentions latency + errors started after a large batch ingestion (embedding job) they kicked off. Could be thundering traffic to control-plane routing lookups.

james (platform): that fits. routing-policy does a configdb read per request when cache miss. If their embedding job hammered the API and invalidated caches, we could exhaust configdb connections.

samir (runtime): reproducer: curl to hosted endpoint with same api-key for tenant-acme, and flood with 200 concurrent requests to trigger routing lookups. I got a few 502s and 504s within ~30s. logs show: ```
[error] gateway: upstream error: controlplane:502
[debug] routing-policy -> configdb: query get_policy(tenant_acme) latency=3100ms
```

maya (oncall): immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) enable cached fallback for routing-policy so control-plane can serve last-known-policy when configdb is degraded; 2) temporarily increase configdb conn pool size for control-plane and/or throttle tenant-acme at the gateway. Which do we want to do now?

james (platform): prefer non-invasive first: flip routing-policy fallback to cached for all tenants for 10m, and open a rate limit for tenant-acme. I'll patch the feature-flag.

anna (support): customer asked for ETA — can we do that now?

maya (oncall): applying flag now. opsbot: run rollout toggle routing-policy.cached-fallback=true scope=global ttl=600

opsbot: acknowledged — rollout started, target: control-plane routing-policy, batch=10% -> 100%

maya (oncall): also provisioning a temporary increase to configdb pool: patching helm values for control-plane to pool_max=150 -> previous 80. james, will need approval to scale connections on DB.

james (platform): I approve for 20m emergency bump. opsbot: apply helm patch chart=control-plane values.pool_max=150 annotate=emergency

opsbot: helm apply queued. oncall-bot: alert configured for pool_max rollback in 20m

samir (runtime): after toggling fallback we saw immediate drop in 502s from control-plane — gateway now returning 200/streaming for prior requests. Routing-policy logs: 
```
2026-03-17T09:13:20Z routing-policy INFO serving cached policy tenant=tenant-acme cache_age=42s
```

anna (support): customer confirms reduced errors and lower latency. they still saw a few failed billing events (some token billing calls returned 502) — could that be related?

james (platform): billing stack calls control-plane for tenant metadata during charge events. If control-plane was returning 5xx, billing calls would surface errors (non-idempotent billing attempts flagged). Need to audit failed billing attempts and retry those safely.

maya (oncall): next steps: 1) reconcile billing write failures for tenant-acme (support to coordinate), 2) investigate why configdb pool exhausted — possible leak or more connections from background job, 3) add tenant-level ingress throttling as a long-term control.

anna (support): noted. I'll collect failed billing request ids and open a ticket with finance for potential manual reconciles.

samir (runtime): root-cause hypothesis: large embedding job from tenant-acme generated sustained high concurrency to hosted-api which caused routing-policy cache churn -> many configdb reads -> conn pool exhaustion -> routing-policy timeouts -> control-plane 5xx -> gateway surfaced 502s. Also saw auth-session latency increases; session validation now falls back less gracefully causing client 5xx.

james (platform): follow-up fixes: - add bulk-ingest backpressure guidance in docs - add per-tenant burst limits in gateway - increase default routing-policy cache TTL for low-change tenants - instrument request fanout matrix per tenant for alerting

maya (oncall): I'll create an incident postmortem checklist and schedule a configdb connection leak / usage audit with infra. tagging @infra and @billing.

anna (support): customer update: thanks for fast response, please confirm when billing retries complete. :thumbsup:

james (platform): I'll follow up on billing retry plan and postmortem actions. will file follow-up tickets.

maya (oncall): closing operational loop: opsbot: schedule rollback of pool_max to 80 in 20m unless flagged /manual-extend true

opsbot: scheduled rollback at 09:33 UTC unless extended

anna (support): thanks everyone — marking this thread resolved for support but keeping incident tracking open in #incidents.

samir (runtime): adding one more note for postmortem: capture KV handshake latencies between routing-policy and configdb (we saw spikes) and make them part of control-plane runbook.

james (platform): agreed. I'll add to runbook and link runbook here when ready.

maya (oncall): end of thread — will update #incidents when postmortem is created.
